sentences.text:
The appellant has filed this appeal being aggrieved by the award dated 15.05.2020 passed in MACC No.103/2018 challenging quantum of compensation on two counts; first, the income of the deceased has not been assessed properly and secondly, the multiplier has been applied by considering the age of the deceased as 26 years whereas it should have been considered as 23 years.
2. The factum of accident and liability of the insurance company is not under dispute.
3.
The short facts of the case are that on 10.12.2017 at around 20.45 the deceased Rajesh was going in the Eicher vehicle registration No.MP09-GF- 7157 as cleaner to Ahemdabad.

When the said vehicle reached near village- Chawadia the driver of the said vehicle i.e. respondent No.1 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner because of which the vehicle turned turtle and 2 MA-948-2021 Rajesh @ Ravi died on the spot.
The appellants/claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the claims tribunal for the death of Rajesh in the aforesaid accident.

The claims tribunal after assessing the evidence which were brought on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,22,000/- in which amount of Rs.9,52,000/- was for loss of dependency and Rs.15000/- each for loss of estate and funeral expenses, apart from that an amount of Rs.40,000/-
was awarded for loss of consortium to the wife of the deceased.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income of the deceased has not been assessed correctly.
He submits that the deceased was working as cleaner of the vehicle in which he was sitting at the time of accident.

It was claimed that he was earning Rs.9000/- per month from his job as a cleaner, thus, the claims tribunal has wrongly discarded the said claim and wrongly taken the income of the deceased as Rs.5000/- per month on notional basis by treating him unskilled labourer on daily basis.

In support of his submission, he refers Exs.P-6, P-10, P-11 and P-13 which are lists of documents and letter dated 11.12.2017 of police station-Lunawaada and the details of report sent by police to the civil surgeon along with the dead body.

In all theses documents, the age of the deceased is mentioned as 23 years, thus, he claims that apart from the issue of income, the issue of multiplier Smt Bhuri Bai vs Mithun on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178562270/
1 is also relevant as multiplier should have been taken on the basis of the age as 23 years not as 26 years.

sentences.text: 5. Apart from the above submissions, the counsel for the appellant submits that the deduction for personal expenses at 1/3rd is also not correct 3 MA-948-2021 in view of the fact that there were 4 claimants.
He also submits that the mother was also entitled for amount of compensation for loss of consortium which has not been awarded.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company by referring to the findings recorded in para 64 of the award submits that there was not documentary proof regarding the age of the appellant even Aadhar Card was not produced although the appellant No.1 admitted in her deposition before the Court that Aadhar Card of the deceased was available.
Although AW-1 accepted in her cross-examination that Aadhar Card of the deceased was available.

As regards the income, the counsel for insurance company refers to findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 15 of the impugned award and submits that it has specifically been recorded by the claims tribunal in para 15 that although the appellants/claimants have claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.9000/- per month but the owner of the vehicle and even the driver of the offending vehicle have denied this fact in their reply to the claim petition and it has been asserted that he was receiving Rs.100/- per day.
7.

On the question of 1/3rd for personal expenses, learned counsel for the appellants submits that out of the 4 claimants, 2 are elder brother and younger sister and cannot be treated to be dependents of the deceased.
In fact, there is a clear finding in para 13 that the elder brother was earning member of the family and sister Sumitra was being taken care of from the income of the said elder brother.
Thus, the deduction of 1/3rd is correct and proper.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9. From the pleadings in the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act it is clear that the appellants/claimants themselves have mentioned the age of the deceased as 26 years.
The appellant No.1 while recording her statement in the court has also claimed that the deceased was 26 years of age at the time of accident.
Merely on the basis of some documents prepared by the Gujrat police writing the age of the deceased as 23 years, it cannot be presumed that he was 23 years of age.
The claimants/appellants have themselves pleaded before the claims tribunal that the deceased was 26 years of age.
Thus, there was no reason to interfere with the findings recorded by the claims tribunal regarding the age of the deceased as 26 years.
Even if we see the age of the wife of the deceased then also the claim petition was filed on 31.08.2023 when the age of the wife is written as 24 years.
Thus, for this reason also the assessment of the age of the deceased 26 years appears to be correct.

10. As regards the income of the deceased, it has been stated by the appellants that the deceased was earning Rs.9000/- per month but the same was denied by the owner of the vehicle as well as driver.

2

The appellants/claimants have not produced any material to prove that the deceased was earning Rs.9000/- per month, thus, on this count also the findings of the claims tribunal recorded in para 15 of the impugned award are not interfered with.

As regards the issue of dependency, the claims tribunal has clearly recorded the findings in para 13 which are based on cross examination of AW-1,
wife of the deceased that the elder brother of the 5 MA-948-2021 deceased was already earning form the period before the death of Rajesh, thus, he cannot be treated to be dependent on the deceased- Rajesh.
It has also been accepted by her that the sister of the deceased was also being taken care of by the elder brother of the deceased.
In view of the above, the deduction of 1/3rd for personal expenses is also found to be correct.
11. As regards the claim of consortium, it is seen from para 20 of the award that the amount of Rs.40000/- has been awarded for loss of consortium.
Though, there are 4 claimants but out of the four claimants, Bhuri Bai i.e. the claimant/appellant No.1 and Champa Bai/appellant No.2 are wife and mother of the deceased.
Thus, both of them are entitled for compensation for loss of consortium.
It is thus held that apart from amount of Rs.40,000/- awarded to wife, the mother is also entitled for compensation for loss of consortium at Rs.40,000/-.
12. In view of the above analysis, the appeal of the appellants/claimants fails except for the amount of Rs.40,000/- in above terms.
The mother i.e. appellant No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- over and above the amount of compensation awarded by the claims tribunal.
The same shall be paid with interest @6% per annum from the date of presentation of the claim petition before the claims tribunal.
13. With the above terms, the appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
